title: How much does a trip to Antarctica cost?
summary: See how much a trip to Antarctica costs from five regions, with cruise fares, flights to Ushuaia and a budget range for each. Compare.
body_markdown:
Glaciers, freezing temperatures, and dramatic landscapes are no longer enough for me. Ever[since I visited Iceland](https://grey.co/blog/trip-to-iceland-cost) I’ve had another icy destination on my mind: Antarctica. I want to go even further south to see penguins, enormous blue icebergs and almost no signs of civilisation. I’m most excited to see humpback whales surfacing while on the water.


I've been planning this trip for over a year now. And by planning, I mean researching expedition companies, comparing cabins, watching videos of the Drake Passage and trying to understand why two seemingly similar cruises can have a $10,000 price difference.


Antarctica is definitely not a cheap holiday, as it has no commercial airports for frequent travel. But after all this research, I've realised there are ways to make it more affordable. So here's what I've found, from actual expedition prices to flights, accommodation and all those other things to pay for that aren't immediately obvious.


A trip to Antarctica costs roughly $9,000 to $25,000 per person. Most trips are expedition cruises from Ushuaia in Argentina, though last-minute deals and shared cabins can lower the total; the cruise alone runs between $8,000 and $15,000, plus flights to Ushuaia and a night or two before departure.


Here's what you should budget for if you're also dreaming of visiting the seventh continent.


## How much does a trip to Antarctica cost? Budget range overview


Derek Oyen/Unsplash


The biggest expense is the expedition cruise itself. Unlike a regular holiday, you can't simply book a flight to Antarctica, find a hotel and explore independently. Most visitors travel aboard expedition ships departing from Ushuaia, Argentina, with trips lasting around 10 to 12 days. Your ship is your accommodation, restaurant and transport throughout the expedition.


Based on published prices for the 2026–27 season, here's what different types of trips can cost.


Type of Antarctica trip Cruise cost per person


Budget expedition, shared cabin or promotional fare $7,000–$10,000


Standard expedition cruise $10,000–$15,000


Premium expedition cruise $15,000–$25,000


Luxury expedition $25,000–$35,000+


Consider these as planning ranges, not fixed prices. For example, Oceanwide Expeditions lists some March 2027 departures from $7,800 per person, with selected promotional cabins priced lower. Meanwhile, Quark Expeditions has November 2026 voyages with discounted cabin prices starting above $13,000.


The difference often comes down to the ship, cabin, itinerary, season and activities included. Most expedition fares cover accommodation, meals, guided Zodiac excursions, onboard lectures and some equipment. You also have to consider a little extra for flights to Argentina, additional hotels, insurance and optional activities.


There's something I hadn’t considered while putting my plans together: not every cruise to Antarctica lets you actually step onto the continent. Per the International Association of Antarctica Tour Operators (IAATO), ships carrying more than 500 passengers cannot make landings. If walking among penguins and exploring the coastline is part of your dream, check the ship's landing arrangements before booking.
And if you're still figuring out how to afford a big holiday, here's a useful guide on[how to plan a trip on a budget](https://grey.co/blog/plan-a-trip-on-a-budget) .


## How much does a trip to Antarctica cost from the USA?


Dylan Shaw/Unsplash


If you're travelling from the United States, you'll usually fly to Buenos Aires, Argentina, before taking a domestic flight to Ushuaia, the southernmost city in Argentina. Flights from major US cities such as New York, Miami and Los Angeles can vary considerably depending on the season and how early you book.


Here's a reasonable starting budget:


Expense Estimated cost


Return flights from the USA to Ushuaia $1,200–$2,500


Antarctica expedition cruise $8,000–$15,000


Hotels, meals and other expenses $500–$1,500


Estimated total $9,700–$19,000


You may find cheaper flights from Miami or New York than from smaller US cities. Also, some expedition packages include flights between Buenos Aires and Ushuaia, so check what's already covered. These estimates assume a standard expedition rather than a luxury cruise.


I'd personally allow at least one night in Ushuaia before departure, preferably two. Missing your cruise because of a delayed flight is an expensive travel mistake.


## How much does a trip to Antarctica cost from North America?


For travellers from Canada, Mexico and other parts of North America, the journey is the same: you'd fly to Argentina, connect to Ushuaia and then get aboard your expedition ship. If you're travelling from Canada, you'll also need to consider the exchange rate between Canadian dollars and the currency used to price your cruise.


Expense Estimated cost


Return flights to Ushuaia $1,300–$2,600


Antarctica expedition cruise $8,000–$15,000


Hotels, meals and extras $500–$1,500


Estimated total $9,800–$19,100


Most expedition operators publish their fares in USD, so the final cost in your home currency may change between when you start putting your plans together and when you pay. Another thing to check is your flight connection. Depending on your departure city, travelling through the US or another Latin American city may offer different prices.


## How much does a trip to Antarctica cost from Europe?


*Jean Pierre Cabáni* /Unsplash


Travelling from Europe means a longer journey, but there are plenty of flight connections to Argentina from cities such as Madrid, Paris, London and Frankfurt. Spain can be particularly convenient because of its connections with Buenos Aires. For planning purposes, I'd budget €1,300 to €2,500 for return flights to Ushuaia, though prices vary widely depending on your departure city and travel dates.


Expense Estimated cost


Return flights to Ushuaia €1,300–€2,500


Antarctica expedition cruise $8,000–$15,000


Hotels, meals and extras $500–$1,500


The cruise is usually priced in USD, so I wouldn't combine these figures into a euro total without checking the exchange rate when booking.


If you're travelling from Europe, it's worth comparing separate tickets to Buenos Aires and Ushuaia against a single through-ticket. It’s also worth checking the arrival time of both flights; this way, you have time to get between connecting flights.


Also check baggage allowances. Expedition clothing can take up quite a bit of luggage space, although some operators provide waterproof boots and parkas.


## How much does a trip to Antarctica cost from Africa?


For travellers from Africa, reaching Ushuaia can be one of the more complicated parts of the journey.


Depending on your departure country, you may need connections through Europe, the Middle East or South America. Travellers from South Africa may have different routing options from those departing Nigeria, Ghana or Kenya.


Here's an estimated budget:


Expense Estimated cost


Return flights to Ushuaia $1,500–$3,000


Antarctica expedition cruise $8,000–$15,000


Hotels, meals and extras $500–$1,500


Estimated total $10,000–$19,500


Because of the longer journey, I'd consider spending an extra night or two in Argentina before the cruise. You should also check visa and transit requirements carefully. These depend on your passport and the countries you connect through, not simply where you live. And if your expedition company offers an Argentina flight package, compare it against booking everything independently. Sometimes the convenience is worth the extra cost.


## How much does a trip to Antarctica cost from South America?


Here’s one advantage of living in South America: you're already much closer to the departure point. If you're travelling from Brazil, Chile, Uruguay or another neighbouring country, flights to Argentina are generally shorter than those from Europe or North America.


This can make a noticeable difference to your overall budget.


Expense Estimated cost


Return flights to Ushuaia $400–$1,200


Antarctica expedition cruise $8,000–$15,000


Hotels, meals and extras $400–$1,200


Estimated total $8,800–$17,400


Of course, the actual cost depends on your departure city. If you're already in Argentina, you may only need a domestic flight to Ushuaia. Travellers from Brazil can compare connections through Buenos Aires with other available routes.


One thing I'd keep in mind is the Argentine summer holiday season. Flights and accommodation tends to become more expensive around December and January as the holidays peak. For me, this is one of the more encouraging discoveries from my research. The expedition is still expensive, but being closer to Argentina means there's at least one part of the budget where I might save money.


## Trip to Antarctica cost breakdown: Cruise, flights, gear and extras


After looking at dozens of itineraries, I've learnt that the advertised cruise price is only part of the story.


Some operators include flights, hotels and equipment. Others charge separately for almost everything beyond the expedition itself.


Here's a more detailed breakdown of what to budget.


Expense Estimated cost per person


Antarctica expedition cruise $8,000–$15,000


Return flights to Ushuaia $400–$3,000


Pre-cruise hotel, 1–2 nights $100–$400


Meals and transport in Argentina $100–$250


Thermal clothing and gear $150–$500


Travel and medical evacuation insurance $200–$600


Tips and personal expenses $100–$300


Optional activities $300–$2,000+


*These are illustrative planning allowances, not live quotes. Some costs may already be included in your cruise fare.*


### The cruise: Where most of your money goes


The ship makes the biggest difference to your Antarctica vacation cost. Oceanwide's 2026–27 published fares include standard Antarctic Peninsula departures starting around $9,650, with selected March discounts; some cabins are priced as low as $8,000. Quark's published November 2026 prices include 11-day voyages starting around $13,500 with promotional discounts. These are real advertised fares, but availability can change quickly.


The cabin also matters. Sharing a cabin with other passengers can save thousands compared with booking a private suite. If you're travelling alone, check whether the operator offers shared cabins without a single supplement. Otherwise, you could end up paying considerably more.


### Flights and accommodation in Argentina


Most people travel through Buenos Aires before continuing to Ushuaia. You may need to change airports in Buenos Aires, depending on your international and domestic flights, so leave enough time between connections. I'd also budget for at least one night before departure. Some operators actually require you to arrive a day early.


If your package includes a hotel or domestic flight, don't add those costs twice.


### Clothing and equipment


Antarctica is cold, but you don't necessarily need to buy an entirely new wardrobe. You'll want thermal base layers, waterproof trousers, warm socks, gloves and layers that work together.
jusMany expedition companies provide waterproof boots, and some include a parka you can keep.


### Insurance and optional activities


This is one expense I wouldn't try to minimise too aggressively.


Antarctica is remote, and medical evacuation can be extremely expensive. Expedition operators commonly require travel insurance with adequate medical and evacuation cover.


Check the exact minimum coverage required by your operator before purchasing a policy.


Optional activities can also add quite a bit to your budget.


For example, Quark lists sea kayaking at $1,995 on some 2026 expeditions, while camping can cost around $495. Some Oceanwide itineraries include activities such as kayaking and camping in the cruise fare. If there's an activity you particularly want to try, compare what's included rather than looking only at the cabin price.


## How to budget and pay for your trip to Antarctica


After more than a year of planning, I've realised that Antarctica isn't really a trip you book casually. At least, not with my budget.


The most useful approach I've found is to treat it as a longer-term financial goal.


### Set a realistic target


Instead of saving only for the cheapest advertised cruise, I'd build a budget that includes flights, insurance, accommodation and some extra money for unexpected expenses.


For example, if your target is $12,000 and you have 18 months to save, you'd need to put aside approximately $667 per month.


If you have two years, that drops to $500 per month.


Here's how different savings targets compare:


Trip budget Save over 12 months Save over 24 months


$10,000 $833/month $417/month


$12,000 $1,000/month $500/month


$15,000 $1,250/month $625/month


$20,000 $1,667/month $833/month


*These figures are rounded up and assume no interest or investment returns.* If you already have money saved, your monthly target will be lower.


### Keep your Antarctica budget separate


If you're saving for a trip priced in USD, keeping that money separate from everyday spending can make it easier to track your progress.

## Is Antarctica worth the cost?


I haven't made it there yet, so I can't give you a first-hand verdict. But after researching this trip for more than a year, I understand why people are willing to spend so much to experience it.


It's not just another holiday destination. It's the possibility of seeing a landscape that looks almost untouched, watching penguins in their natural habitat and experiencing a part of the world that relatively few people get to visit. And I think that's what keeps me planning, even when the prices make me reconsider my entire travel budget.


My advice is to give yourself time, compare expedition companies carefully and pay attention to what's included. A cheaper cruise isn't necessarily better value if you end up paying extra for everything you want to do.

## Frequently asked questions about travelling to Antarctica


### How much does a trip to Antarctica cost?


A typical Antarctica trip costs around $9,000 to $25,000 per person, including an expedition cruise, flights and other expenses. Budget shared-cabin deals can bring the cost down, while luxury expeditions can exceed $30,000 per person.


### Can you visit Antarctica cheaply?


The cheapest way to visit Antarctica is usually to book a discounted expedition cruise, share a cabin or travel during the beginning or end of the season. Some 2026–27 promotional fares have been advertised below $8,000 per person, excluding international flights and other expenses.


### How long is a cruise to Antarctica?


Most classic Antarctic Peninsula cruises last around 10 to 12 days, including the crossing from Ushuaia. Longer trips visiting South Georgia or the Falkland Islands can last two to three weeks or more.


### When is the best time to visit Antarctica?


The main tourist season runs from November to March, during the Antarctic summer. December and January offer long daylight hours, while February and March can be particularly appealing for whale watching. Conditions and wildlife sightings vary throughout the season.


### Can you fly to Antarctica instead of taking a cruise?


Yes. Some expedition companies offer fly-cruise itineraries that use charter flights between Punta Arenas in Chile and King George Island in Antarctica. These can reduce time spent crossing the Drake Passage, but they are often more expensive and remain subject to weather delays.


### Do you need a visa to visit Antarctica?


Antarctica doesn't have a conventional tourist visa system, but you may need visas or transit permissions for Argentina, Chile or other countries on your route. Your expedition operator handles relevant Antarctic authorisations, while entry requirements depend on your nationality.


### Is travel insurance required for Antarctica?


Most expedition operators require adequate travel medical and emergency evacuation insurance. Coverage requirements vary, so check your operator's policy before purchasing insurance. Ordinary travel insurance may not cover polar expeditions or certain adventure activities.
